Children's ibuprofen recall: what happened and what to do

If you bought Corvane children's ibuprofen (berry, 100 mg/5 mL, 120 mL bottle) from us, please read this whole post.

What happened
The problem is the syringe in the box, not the medicine. The numbers printed on the syringe barrel are wrong. Every mark holds double what it says. The line marked 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL, and the line marked 5 mL actually measures 10 mL. A parent following the label exactly would give twice the intended dose.

The medicine itself is fine. It is not contaminated and it is not expired (expiry 08/2027). The recall is only about the syringe.

Which boxes
Lots CV6114A and CV6114B. The lot number is printed on the bottom of the box. If your bottle has a different lot number, this recall does not apply to it.

What to do
1. Check the lot number on the bottom of the box.
2. If it is one of those two lots, do not use the syringe that came in the box. Throw it out.
3. Come in for a correctly marked replacement syringe (details below).

If your child may have been given too much
Call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017 right away. Tell them your child's age and weight, how much was given, and when. We can't tell from a Facebook post whether a particular child is okay. It depends on weight, how many doses were given, and how the kidneys are doing. The poison centre will assess your child, so if you have any doubt about the dose, please call.

Do not give another dose until the poison centre or your doctor says it's okay.

Go to the ER or call 911 if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

What we are doing
- New syringes are arriving from our supplier today before noon. They are free for anyone who needs one, and you don't need a receipt.
- If you would rather return the bottle, you can get a full refund through the product recall.
- We will be open extra hours this Saturday, 10 to 4, for exchanges.
- We received the recall notice on Nov 6. We took the remaining bottles off the shelf and put signs up on Nov 7. Over-the-counter sales don't come with a phone number, so we could not call people directly. That is why I'm posting this here.

Please share this with anyone you know who bought this product. If you have questions, come in or call us and one of the pharmacists will talk to you.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy
